title: docs: three Expanding Frontiers idea tournaments and their execution DAGs
body:
## Summary

Runs the repository's own GenericPrompt Ultimate Solution Tournament
(`prompts/shared/ULTIMATE_SOLUTION_TOURNAMENT.md`) three times against non-software
subjects, each with a rubric rebuilt per section 4 rather than reused:

| # | Directory | Subject | Winner |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `docs/plan/expanding-frontiers-tournament-2026-08-28/` | Which idea most likely wins an [Expanding Frontiers](https://www.expandingfrontiers.org) grant or award | **Frontier Assurance** 8.79 |
| B | `docs/plan/expanding-frontiers-whitespace-and-youth-2026-08-28/` | Which idea that essentially **nobody is doing** wins one | **Boom Baseline** 9.12 |
| C | same directory | Which idea a **high school student** can personally pitch and execute at the ExF Space Entrepreneur Summer Academy | **The Boom Map** 9.34 |

Full podiums:

- **A:** Frontier Assurance 8.79 (a sealed flight recorder for autonomous operations) · CryoAssay 8.02 · Saltline 6.84
- **B:** Boom Baseline 9.12 (the independent launch overpressure record) · Peninsula 8.39 · SARGO 7.79
- **C:** The Boom Map 9.34 (a student-built overpressure sensor network) · Beach Fuel 8.58 · Closure Count 8.39

Each run ships a reproducible scorer, a machine-readable result set with sensitivity
analysis, a source register with per-claim confidence levels and open evidence
obligations, an execution DAG with full section-17 node contracts, a validator, and a
section-42 handoff.

**Risks / TODOs / gaps:** run A's winner is **not robust** — two of six sensitivity
variants flip it to CryoAssay, and the report leads with that table rather than
burying it. Runs B and C are robust across nine variants, but rest on a weaker
premise: their heaviest criterion, whitespace at 0.20, is scored from a **failure to
find** a competitor in a web search, which is close to the weakest evidence there is.
Twelve evidence obligations (O1-O12) are open because several primary-source fetches
were blocked by the executing environment's egress proxy, including the ExF
competition rules themselves, so the judging criteria throughout are **derived, not
quoted**. Two cited figures sit at confidence C and are flagged as unusable in a pitch
until verified. Runs B and C also carry a real non-technical risk discussed openly in
their report section 4: both winners measure a launch operator's impact on its
neighbours, in a region where roughly 80 of those neighbours are suing that operator,
and whether ExF hears that as coexistence infrastructure or as adversarial is an open
question that must be asked before submitting, not guessed.

## Governance tier

- [x] Governance-lite: documentation-only correction with no behavior, product-claim,
  acceptance-criterion, security, architecture, policy, courtroom, or schema change.
- [ ] Governed: all other changes.

**Why it qualifies.** Additive documentation and four standalone analysis scripts in
two new `docs/plan/` directories. Nothing outside those directories is touched. No
product runtime, policy, schema, controller, `.autopilot/` content, acceptance
criterion, or product superiority claim changes. The scripts import only the standard
library, are imported by no product module, and are not part of the CI gate. Nothing
asserts a capability of Hive Mind OS; run A describes the repository only as an asset
the entrant already owns, quoting its README's own prototype-status disclaimer
verbatim, and runs B and C drop founder advantage from the rubric entirely.

## Validation

- `score_tournament.py` and `score_tournaments.py` regenerate all three result sets
  deterministically. 30 + 24 + 20 = 74 entrants scored.
- `validate_dag.py` (both directories) passes on all three DAGs: dependencies resolve,
  acyclic, every level strictly later than its dependencies, each irreversible node
  alone at its level, critical paths are real dependency chains, and all 27 section-17
  contract fields present on every node. **This validator caught two genuine defects**
  on first run in directory A — two nodes placed in the same level as their own
  dependencies, the "a dependency level is not an executable wave" defect from
  `docs/execution/runbooks/PRODUCT-GENERIC-DAG.md` lesson 4. Both repaired, correction
  recorded in the plan's `notes`.
- Fifteen rubric-sensitivity variants computed across the three tournaments and stored
  under `sensitivity` in the result JSON. Two flip run A's winner; none flips B or C.
- A hand-asserted sensitivity figure in an early draft of run A was found wrong on
  computation and corrected; the finding changed that report's headline confidence.
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` — **not meaningful here and not claimed as
  passing.** It reports 96 errors on the unmodified tree because the package is not
  installed (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hive_mind_os'`). Verified identical
  before and after; the diff adds no test and imports no product module.

## Safety

- [x] No credentials, private data, or unrelated generated artifacts are included.
- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Anticipated questions

**Why does this belong in this repository?** It exercises the repo's own reusable
prompt asset against subjects far outside software architecture, three times, and that
produced a reusable finding recorded in the plans: the generic DAG defect classes
catalogued in `PRODUCT-GENERIC-DAG.md` reproduce in non-software DAGs. That is evidence
for the "these are repo-independent" claim that runbook makes. It follows the
established `docs/plan/genericprompt-execution-2026-08-09/` precedent for this artefact
type.

**Is run A's winner a rationalisation for the author's own codebase?** Section 2.1
exists to answer that honestly rather than defensively. `founder_unfair_advantage`
carries 0.10; zero it and the margin collapses from 0.770 to **0.078**, which the
report calls a tie rather than a win. Remove both prize-physics criteria and CryoAssay
wins outright at 8.974 to 8.449. Runs B and C then drop that criterion entirely, and
neither picks a software company — which is itself the check working.

**Why is "nobody is doing it" scored at all, given the evidence problem?** Because it
was the question asked. The mitigation is structural rather than rhetorical: an
**emptiness classification** gates every entrant before scoring, and two classes
disqualify — `EMPTY_BECAUSE_BAD` (empty because it does not work or has no buyer) and
`NOT_ACTUALLY_EMPTY`. Eleven of 44 entrants across B and C were removed that way,
including the four most common high school space projects in existence. Scoring
emptiness without asking why it is empty is how a tournament rewards a trap, and this
is the mechanism that stops it. The residual risk is stated at the top of the source
register rather than in a footnote, and node `WS-000` exists solely to attack the
claim.

**Why four scripts instead of Markdown tables?** So the conclusions are falsifiable. A
reviewer who disagrees edits a score and reruns; ranking, elimination record and
sensitivity all move together. This PR contains direct evidence of why that matters,
in the corrected sensitivity figure above.

**Why a local `validate_dag.py` rather than `.autopilot/bin/dag_standard.py`?** The
controller bundle is sealed and out of scope, and its linter is bound to controller
plan shapes rather than arbitrary planning documents under `docs/plan/`. The local
validator is ~81 lines of standard library checking only these files. Honestly, it is
defence-in-depth if these plans are ever controller-installed; it is load-bearing today
because nothing else validates a `docs/plan/` graph, and it caught two real defects.

**What integration cost does this impose?** None. No shared file, schema, key or enum
is touched; nothing outside the two new directories is read or written; no module
imports the scripts; the CI gate is unchanged.

**Does anything fail open?** No. Every irreversible action — two submissions and one
publication — is marked `irreversible`, sits alone at its own level, and depends on an
independent review by someone who did not author the work. `validate_dag.py` asserts
the alone-at-its-level property mechanically, so removing a gate fails the validator
rather than passing quietly. A skipped review fails **closed**.

## Context for an AI agent

**Why this exists.** The owner asked, on a branch off latest `main`, for the top three
ideas to enter into Expanding Frontiers and for the "subject DAG" to pick the best one
for winning a grant or award; then for ideas nobody else is doing, and for the same
exercise scoped to a high school student. "Subject DAG" resolves to
`prompts/shared/ULTIMATE_SOLUTION_TOURNAMENT.md`, whose header field is literally
`SUBJECT: [INSERT SUBJECT]` and whose Part II converts a winner into an execution DAG.

**File relationships.** Each directory's scorer is the only source of its numbers; the
result JSON is generated and must never be hand-edited. `FULL_REPORT.md` narrates what
the scorer computes and must be kept consistent with it — change a score, rerun, then
update the report's result and sensitivity sections. `SOURCE_REGISTER.md` is the
evidence spine; every factual claim cites an `S`-numbered entry. Directory B's register
continues directory A's numbering (S20-S29, O8-O12) and A's entries still apply.

**The substantive findings, for whoever picks this up.**

1. *Run A:* the two strongest single ideas finished 0.01 apart and are near-perfect
   complements — each one's fatal weakness is the other's strength. That is what made
   hybridisation worth doing rather than decorative.
2. *Run B:* the **highest-whitespace idea lost.** The launch-site-by-LNG-terminal
   hazard model scored a perfect 10 on whitespace and topped the originals at 8.630,
   then took a round-3 score of 3 because it is `EMPTY_BECAUSE_GATED` — modelling it
   needs facility data from two operators who will not hand it over. The winning hybrid
   reaches that gated space by deploying a sensor network nobody's permission is
   required for, then owning the only independent dataset the gatekeepers lack.
3. *Runs B and C:* the venture winner and the youth winner occupy **the same gap at
   different scales**, which is itself evidence the gap is real, and the student's
   dataset is genuinely the seed of the commercial one.

**Kept deliberately honest — please do not "fix" these.** Several primary-source
fetches were blocked by the egress proxy (`expandingfrontiers.org`,
`exfspacetechppitchcomp2024.org`, `airforcetimes.com`). Per `AGENTS.md` courtroom rule
10 nothing from those pages was reconstructed from memory; they are logged as
obligations and appear as gating nodes. The $32,000 prize figure is confidence **B**
from a prior-cycle site; the AFRL programme specifics are confidence **C** from a
single aggregator; the S24 whitespace finding is a **negative** search result. None may
be promoted without a new primary source. Run B's report also scores SARGO down to 5
on "emptiness is not a trap" because sargassum bioaccumulates arsenic and the digestate
carries it — the charismatic idea is penalised for a real chemistry problem rather than
promoted for being a good story.

**Known incompleteness, reported rather than hidden.** In run A one hybrid scores
exactly the same as its own core component, meaning the combination added nothing. In
each run a deliberately over-broad hybrid was entered and lost, testing whether breadth
beats focus in a five-minute pitch. It does not.
